patch.description:
Correct a conference's details.

There was no write path of any kind here. A conference could be
created and deleted, and nothing in between — so a scraped row's
dates, location, venue or cost could never be fixed, and the
extraction LLM's answer was final. Most rows come from the scraper,
which makes "the machine guessed and you cannot argue" the normal
case rather than the edge case.

Only fields explicitly present in the request body are written
(``exclude_unset``), so sending ``{"venue": "Hall 4"}`` cannot blank
out the dates. Passing an explicit null DOES clear a field, which is
how you undo a bad extraction.

``status`` is deliberately not editable here — that is a decision,
and decisions go through /decisions so they get a Decision row and an
audit entry rather than being quietly overwritten.

raw_pages-via-conference_sources). The single DELETE cascades; we
log the deletion afterwards so admins
have an audit trail.

are entirely absent is dropped and the rest renormalised — so the
numbers only add up if the caller can see which weights applied.

Rank the active talk library against this conference.

Deliberately a separate ranking from ``/smes``: CFP committees accept
a talk first and a speaker second, so the operator wants "which of our
talks fits this event" and "who should go" as two independent lists.
The similarity is the same top-K-cosine measure the SME bio dimension
uses, so the two lists' numbers are comparable.

AnalyticsOverview.title: AnalyticsOverview
AnalyticsOverview.description:
Chart-ready series, pre-binned server-side.

The frontend draws axes and bars; it never aggregates. Each list is a
series of {label-ish key, numeric value(s)} points whose exact keys
differ per chart — hence the permissive ChartPoint.

AttendanceSummary.title: AttendanceSummary
AttendanceSummary.description:
The event-level facts, edited as one form alongside the people.

Every field is optional and stays answerable later. The operator
records cost and leads when they have them, which is usually weeks
after the event — a form that refused to save without them would just
mean nothing gets recorded at all.

owner_id.description: The existing entity to attach to.

BoostBreakdownRead.description: Why the live score differs from the stored blend.

ConferenceCreate.title: ConferenceCreate
ConferenceCreate.description: POST /conferences payload. Slug is server-derived from name+year.

ConferenceCreateResponse.title: ConferenceCreateResponse
ConferenceCreateResponse.description:
Return shape for POST /conferences — the new row plus the matcher
verdict from the auto-run that fires right after the insert commit.

ConferenceListItem.title: ConferenceListItem
ConferenceListItem.description: List-row shape — adds matcher scores from the latest match row.

ConferenceUpdate.title: ConferenceUpdate
ConferenceUpdate.description:
PATCH /conferences/{id} payload — correcting a conference.

Every field is optional, and the route writes only what the caller
actually sent (``exclude_unset``). That distinction matters: sending
``{"venue": "Hall 4"}`` must not blank the dates, while sending
``{"venue": null}`` must clear the venue. A model where "absent" and
"null" mean the same thing cannot express "undo a bad extraction".

``status`` is absent on purpose. Changing it is a decision, and
decisions go through POST /decisions so they produce a Decision row
and an audit entry. An edit form that could quietly flip an approval
would be the same defect the decay pass had, with a human driving.

``slug`` is absent too — it is derived identity, and rewriting it
would orphan the dedup key that stops the same conference being
ingested twice.

only_ai.description: Filter the feed to keyword-matching events only. Off by default: measured against the live feed this filter dropped 375 of 801 future events, including conferences for our own projects. Turn on only if the list genuinely floods.

future_only.description: Skip events whose start_date is in the past.

limit.description: Cap how many filtered events get persisted this run. Null = unlimited.

batch_limit.description: Stop after geocoding this many rows. Null = walk every row with a city and no coordinates yet. The Nominatim policy is 1 req/sec, so 500 rows ≈ 9 minutes.

Relaxed preview returned by the PDF upload endpoint.

No min_length constraints — the LLM may not extract every field perfectly.
The operator reviews and edits before saving via the normal create endpoint.

MessagingDocumentCreate.description: POST body. Accepts both structured and pdf source types.

PillarAnalytics.title: PillarAnalytics
PillarAnalytics.description:
Pillar performance from participation + outcome data.

A conference aligned to two pillars counts toward both — these are
per-pillar views, so sums must never be totalled across pillars.

PillarConferenceItem.title: PillarConferenceItem
PillarConferenceItem.description:
One conference ranked against a pillar.

``pillar_score`` is this pillar's own alignment edge (conference_pillars,
written by the matcher), NOT the conference's top-pillar assignment — so
each pillar page gets its own ordering of the same corpus.
``overall_score`` is the live blend, identical to what the conference
list and detail pages show.

warning.default: Contains secret API keys in plain text. Store with chmod 600, never commit to git, never share.

SettingsBackup.title: SettingsBackup
SettingsBackup.description:
The export shape. Includes secret values in plain text.

Treat the file as sensitive — it contains the LLM API key. Save with
chmod 600, don't commit to git, don't share in chat.

skip_unknown.title: Skip Unknown
skip_unknown.description: If true, silently skip keys not in the current settings spec (e.g. a setting renamed since the export). If false, 400 on unknown keys.

SmeExternalLinks.title: SmeExternalLinks
SmeExternalLinks.description: Allowed link keys for an SME profile. Add new keys here with intent.

SmeRead.title: SmeRead
SmeRead.description:
SME row as returned by the API.

Inherits the field set from ``SmeBase`` but **relaxes** the
min-length constraints on the four fields that ``SmeBase`` requires
on write. The read surface has to be able to serialize any row
already in the DB — including partially-seeded rows uploaded via
a bulk import with placeholder bios + empty topic/audience arrays,
which is a deliberate "fill in later" workflow.

Strict validation still applies on ``SmeCreate`` / ``SmeUpdate``.

SourceKind.description: Crawl-strategy enum. Pass 1 ships rss + page; pass 2 adds the rest.
